summary: Atomic optimizer-config snapshot/restore and per-tenant gating assistance after mixed-opt changes caused stream truncation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NovaHealth reported that after a targeted optimizer-profile migration for a small set of tenants, a subset of streaming responses were truncated mid-stream and some requests returned 499 client disconnects. This began immediately after a staged opt-config push that enabled a mixed-quant + aggressive KV-prefetch profile for their workload.

Impact:
- Several NovaHealth integration endpoints experienced truncated streaming sessions for ~12% of requests to their /chat/stream route.
- Tail latency increased from 180ms to 1.2s for affected tenants.
- No token-level quality regressions reported, but user-facing sessions were interrupted.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated cluster (dedicated pool for NovaHealth) in prod us-west-2.
- Model: redwood-lm-3b-v2 pinned.
- Opt-profile applied via central config-service (staged rollout: tenant gating, 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 90m).

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Use NovaHealth tenant API key and send streaming chat requests with frequent short prompts (~30 tokens).
2) Observe that ~1 in 8 streams terminates early with client-side disconnect and server-side 499.
3) Reverting opt-profile at tenant level appears to restore prior behavior.

Logs / Observations:
- Serving-runtime logs show intermittent KV cache eviction spikes and a correlated increase in upstream send buffer full events.
- Traces show a subset of requests hit a mix of kernel paths (quantized + prefetch) and experienced unexpected loopback on the per-request router creating a fast-path abort.
- No underlying GPU OOMs.

Customer request:
- Assistance to safely snapshot current opt-config state, perform an atomic restore to pre-change profile for affected tenants, and guidance on per-tenant gating best practices to avoid rollout blast radius.

Workaround attempted by customer:
- Manual removal of tenant opt override restored normal behavior. Customer requests a reproducible, supported procedure they can follow in future and confirmation we will investigate root cause.

investigation_notes:
Timeline and findings:
- 2026-03-05: Initial reports and sample IDs collected.
- 2026-03-05: SRE captured LB and runtime metrics; observed 499s and write stalls.
- 2026-03-06: Eng reproduced a race locally when opt-profile toggles mid-request; root cause: kernel selection path lacked an in-flight request guard when prefix-KV cache eviction and quantized kernel selection coincided.
- Hypothesis: The staged rollout exposed a rare state where a request saw a config delta mid-eviction, causing the runtime to switch execution paths and drop the streaming write without retry.
- Evidence: runtime trace and flamegraph; matching request IDs across serving-runtime and LB.
- Mitigating action: snapshot current config and perform atomic tenant-level restore.
- Additional observation: higher incidence for short prompts due to tighter batching windows and increased sensitivity to KV cache behavior.

Next steps recommended by Eng team:
1) Merge guard fix in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/412 (adds in-flight request pin during kernel selection).
2) Publish a snapshot/restore runbook for ops and customers with explicit atomicity checks.
3) Update rollout policy: increase initial gating checks, add canary with end-to-end streaming smoke tests, and extend observation window before wider rollout.
4) Create monitoring alert for sudden increase in 499 streaming disconnects and KV eviction rate.
resolution_notes:
Actions performed to resolve:
- Captured a consistent snapshot of NovaHealth opt-config (snap-20260307-nh) before any changes.
- Executed an atomic restore to the pre-migration baseline profile for all NovaHealth tenant IDs during a scheduled low-traffic window (2026-03-07 02:00-02:20 UTC).
- Verified streaming endpoints for customer (end-to-end synthetic smoke tests).
- Monitored tail latency, KV eviction rates, and 499/stream-disconnect counts for 72h post-restore; metrics returned to baseline.
- Eng pushed hotfix PR to add in-flight request guard and a subtle config-change mutex; PR linked above.

Follow-ups and recommendations given to customer:
- Use tenant-level snapshot before any opt-profile changes: run config-service snapshot command and capture the snapshot id.
- For staged rollouts, start with a small canary of 1% tenant traffic and run an automated streaming smoke test for 30m before expanding.
- Avoid combining quantization changes and aggressive KV-prefetch in the same initial canary; separate those changes across independent rollout waves.
- If you need an emergency restore: provide snapshot id and tenant IDs to support and we will execute an atomic restore. Provided documented steps and a one-time assisted runbook to the customer.
- Engineering will schedule the hotfix to roll through Dedicated clusters this week; we will follow up when the fix is in canary and when fully rolled out.
notes_for_ops:
Atomic snapshot/restore checklist (summary):
- Verify snapshot id integrity (sha256) and timestamp.
- Put tenant(s) into maintenance mode to quiesce new long-running streams.
- Execute restore via config-service with --atomic flag.
- Confirm via synthetic streaming smoke test and edge LB logs that 499s have stopped.
- If still present, escalate to runtime oncall and collect traces and per-request kernel selection logs.
- After restore, re-enable staged rollout with separate waves for quantization and KV-prefetch.
